channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Nscale’s $35 Billion IPO Plans Muddied by AI Data Center Delays
item.description: One flagship AI data center in Norway is six months behind schedule, with workers set to be housed in a floating hotel to get it over the finish line.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Solon and Paula Doenecke

item.title: AI Race Heats Up Again a Month After Calls for a Slowdown
item.description: The competition to build more advanced AI remains as fierce as ever.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Don't See Canary in Coal Mine For AI: Khoda
item.description: Neha Khoda, head of US credit strategy at BofA Securities, and Stephanie Doyle, fixed income portfolio manager at JPMorgan Investment Management, join Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield." A measure of CoreWeave’s credit risk climbed to an all-time high Thursday as some of its high-yield bonds extended declines, rattled by the AI cloud-computing company’s talk of tapping vast pools of capital from insurers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What CEOs See as the Biggest Risks to Their Businesses
item.description: Tim Walsh, chairman and CEO at KPMG US, says CEOs broadly recognize AI’s importance and are investing, but measurable business transformation and returns are taking time. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jeff Yan Plans to Bring the Entire Financial Industry onto Hyperliquid
item.description:
In August, President Trump said the CFTC was working on bringing a crypto platform called Hyperliquid into the United States "in a fully compliant and legal fashion.” What exactly is Hyperliquid?
CEO and Co-founder Jeff Yan joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway on the Odd Lots podcast to explain how the platform works and how he plans to bring the entire financial industry onto Hyperliquid. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Music Deals Are Happening, But How Artists Will Be Paid Remains a Mystery
item.description: How exactly AI money will flow through the music industry remains ambiguous
item.dc:creator: Ashley Carman

item.title: Anthropic Stands Alone as Rest of US IPO Market Slows to a Crawl
item.description: A cocktail of risks is threatening to stall the US IPO pipeline, leaving Anthropic PBC’s potential blockbuster debut as one of the few offerings that investors can count on.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Hughes and Bailey Lipschultz

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO Momentum as CoreWeave Rattles AI Trade
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Anthropic's third-quarter revenue numbers as the company gets ready for its IPO. Plus: CoreWeave’s talk of tapping “unlimited” pools of money rattles markets and puts the financing behind the data center buildout back under the microscope; and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says safety and containment should be integrated into AI systems even as AI advances. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inside Blackstone’s Massive Bet on the AI Boom
item.description: Blackstone has built one of Wall Street’s broadest bets on AI, investing across the ecosystem from data centers, power and cooling to chip financing and companies including OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX. Bloomberg’s Preeti Singh explains how President and COO Jon Gray spotted the infrastructure opportunity early and why he sees AI as a generational economic shift that investors can’t afford to ignore. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anduril to Sell Insider Shares at $90 Billion Valuation
item.description: Anduril is allowing employees to sell shares as part of a tender that stands to value the defense technology startup at roughly $90 billion. The tender offer is open to current and former Anduril employees in 16 countries and is set to close on November 9. Bloomberg's Katrina Manson joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: IA y robots humanoides: China desafía el liderazgo de EE.UU.
item.description: El hardware avanzado para robots humanoides es uno de los campos estratégicos de alta tecnología en los que China lleva ventaja sobre EE.UU.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Anthropic 3Q Revenue Hits $16.8 Billion Ahead of IPO
item.description: Anthropic told prospective investors its third-quarter revenue hit $16.8 billion as the artificial intelligence company pushes ahead with plans to go public. Bloomberg's Bailey Lipschultz joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Power On: Is Apple’s HomeView Ecosystem Worth Buying Into?
item.description:
With the newly unveiled HomeView, Apple is finally closing the biggest gap in its ecosystem.
On this episode of the Power On podcast, Mark Gurman talks about Apple's full lineup of devices designed to work together and what it will take to win over consumers already invested in ecosystems offered by rivals like Google and Amazon. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Releases Open AI Model While Keeping Its Best Tech Closed
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. made one of its new artificial intelligence models available for developers to download and modify, while keeping its most advanced technology closed in an effort to convert its AI investments into revenue.
item.dc:creator: Riley Griffin

item.title: Nvidia CEO Downplays CoreWeave Concerns, Bolstering Stock
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang defended the financial health of AI computing supplier CoreWeave Inc., a major customer in which the chipmaker is also an investor, after concerns over its debt sparked a massive selloff of its shares and bonds.
item.dc:creator: Charles Daly and Ian King

item.title: CoreWeave Credit Risk Hits Record as Default Odds Top 60% on Borrowing Plans
item.description: A measure of CoreWeave Inc.’s credit risk climbed to an all-time high Thursday as some of its high-yield bonds extended declines, rattled by the AI cloud-computing company’s talk of tapping vast pools of capital from insurers.
item.dc:creator: Caleb Mutua

item.title: Santander's Ana Botin on US Growth, Debt, AI and the Global Economy | The David Rubenstein Show
item.description: Santander Executive Chair Ana Botin sits down with David Rubenstein to discuss the bank's expansion in the US, including its recent acquisition of Webster Financial, and why she sees lack of economic growth as one of the biggest challenges facing the global economy. She also discusses US debt, the outlook for the US and European economies amid geopolitical uncertainty, and the impact of AI on banking and jobs. Botin is on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This episode was recorded July 13 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Israeli Firms Put Spyware at Al Jazeera via Ads, Report Says
item.description: Two Israeli companies manipulated online advertisements to install surveillance software on dozens of computers at the Qatari news organization Al Jazeera, researchers have found.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gallagher

item.title: Anthropic Revenue Hits $16.8 Billion in Quarter Before IPO
item.description: Anthropic PBC told prospective investors its third-quarter revenue hit $16.8 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, as the artificial intelligence company pushes ahead with plans to go public.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz, Natasha Mascarenhas, Rebecca Torrence and Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Fidelity's Chisholm: Tech Stocks Can Keep ‘Climbing the Wall of Worry’
item.description: Fidelity’s Denise Chisholm says technology stocks have undergone an unusually large valuation reset even as earnings expectations continue to rise, potentially leaving the sector positioned for further gains. She discusses why tech’s roughly 30% multiple contraction may already reflect concerns about slowing AI and technology spending, and why historical data suggests a slowdown in tech capex doesn’t necessarily mean a contraction. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)
